text.p: Dominik Hasek stopped 29 shots and defenceman Garry Galley had a goal and three assists as the Buffalo Sabres beat the Pittsburgh Penguins, 4-1 Thursday.
Hasek made 17 saves in the third period, helping Buffalo improve to 2-4.
At 1-5, the Penguins are off to their worst start since 1983-84, when they lost eight of their first nine games the year before they drafted Mario Lemieux.
In Chicago, Tony Amonte and Chris Chelios scored third-period goals and Ed Belfour made 31 saves as the Chicago Blackhawks edged Detroit, 2-1.
Amonte's goal 18 seconds into the final period lifted Chicago into a 1-1 tie.
Late in the third period, Belfour stopped a couple of long shots by Detroit, which lost any chance at the tying goal when rookie Tomas Holmstrom was penalised for tripping with 50 seconds remaining.

At Colorado, John Vanbiesbrouck stopped 26 shots and Tom Fitzgerald's shorthanded goal in the third period lifted the Florida Panthers to a 2-1 victory over the Colorado Avalanche in the first rematch of last season's Stanley Cup Finals.

Vanbiesbrouck made 15 saves in the first period, two in the second and nine in the third as he kept his league-leading goals-against-average at 0.98. The Panthers, who were swept by Colorado in the Finals, are off to the best start in franchise history and are the NHL's only unbeaten team at 4-0-2.
"I don't think anything other than it's two points for us," said Florida coach Doug MacLean, who downplayed the rematch. "It felt really good, but there's no more than that.
In Dallas, Markus Naslund had two goals and an assist and linemate Mike Ridley added a goal and three assists as the Vancouver Canucks handed the Dallas Stars their first loss of the season, 6-1.
The Stars had won their first six games to set a franchise record, but never got anything going against Vancouver in a fight-filled contest.
In Los Angeles, Ed Olczyk's shorthanded goal broke a second-period tie and Yanic Perreault scored twice as the Los Angeles Kings beat the Boston Bruins, 4-2 for their third straight win.
Barry Potomski stretched the Kings' lead to 3-1 at 8:34 of the third period when he converted Laperriere's centering pass from behind the net.
Boston rallied within a goal on Ted Donato's power-play tally at 13:57, but Perreault scored into an empty net with 34 seconds left to seal the victory.

At the Islanders, Jason Muzzatti made 20 saves in his first start of the season and Kevin Dineen scored twice, leading the Hartford Whalers to their third win in four games, 3-1 over the New York Islanders.
Muzzatti lost a bid for his second career shutout when Derek King scored at 9:53 of the third period.
"The forwards did a great job of keeping the puck on the perimeter and blocking shots," Muzzatti said.
In St Louis, Al MacInnis scored twice and Grant Fuhr made 31 saves as the St. Louis Blues handed the Toronto Maple Leafs their fourth straight loss, 6-1.
The Blues have won three of their last four games and were playing the Maple Leafs for the first time since eliminating them in six games in last season's Western Conference quarterfinals.
"Obviously, Grant Fuhr was without question the number one star," said St. Louis coach Mike Keenan.
The Blues scored three times in a span of 1:43 in the third period with goals from Konstantin Shafranov, Stephane Matteau and MacInnis.
